subject: chemistry
title: Bonding Adventure (Chemistry)
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the three big kinds of bonding: ionic, covalent and metallic.
meta_desc: GCSE Chemistry Bonding foundations — ions, shared electrons, the metallic sea model, with salt, water and copper as examples.
final_note: You learned what ions are, how electrons are shared in covalent bonds, and how a sea of electrons holds metals together.

concepts.def: Atom that has lost or gained electrons; has a charge.
Strong pull between oppositely charged ions.
A shared pair of electrons between two atoms.
Metal ions in a sea of delocalised electrons.
Salt: Na+ and Cl- ions in a giant lattice.
H2O: oxygen sharing electrons with two hydrogens.

walkthroughs.body_html:
In ionic bonding a metal gives electrons to a non-metal.

Sodium loses 1 electron to become Na+. Chlorine gains 1 to become Cl-. The opposite charges pull together to make NaCl — table salt.

Ionic compounds form giant lattices of alternating + and - ions.

Two non-metals don't swap electrons — they share them. A shared pair is one covalent bond.

In H2, two hydrogens share a pair. In H2O, oxygen shares a pair with each of two hydrogens. The result is a molecule.

Metals have a clever trick. Each atom releases its outer electrons into a shared sea. What's left is a regular grid of positive metal ions.

The strong pull between the sea of electrons and the metal ions is the metallic bond. It's why metals are strong and conduct electricity.

mcqs.q: Which bond forms between a metal and a non-metal?
options: Covalent
Ionic
Metallic
Hydrogen

mcqs.q: What is shared in a covalent bond?
options: Protons
Neutrons
A pair of electrons
A nucleus
Metal atoms themselves move to carry the current.
Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
Metals contain naturally moving protons that act as charge carriers.
Delocalised electrons are free to move through the lattice of positive ions, carrying charge.

mcqs.q: Why does graphite conduct electricity but diamond does not?
options: Graphite conducts because it can melt easily at room temperature.
Graphite has delocalised electrons between layers; diamond has all four outer electrons in localised covalent bonds.
Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
Graphite conducts because it is a metal, while diamond is a non-metal.

mcqs.q: What happens to electrons when sodium reacts with chlorine?
options: Sodium and chlorine share an electron between them.
Metals contain naturally moving protons that act as charge carriers.
Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
Sodium loses one electron to chlorine; the resulting Na+ and Cl- ions attract electrostatically.
